sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The window is not a compounder but a refranchising story: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018 [D42][D93], then grew 17.1% in FY2021 and 11.3% in FY2022 [D246][D297].
The FY2017 decline came with a 42.8% drop in Bottling Investments revenue as bottling operations were refranchised [D572][P71].

FY2025 operating income jumped 37.7% [D450], which the filing attributes to lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement, concentrate volume growth of 1% and pricing [P12].
In FY2025 concentrate operations were 59.4% of revenue and contributed 1.6pp of the 1.9% growth, while finished product operations added 0.3pp [D532][D534][D449][D541].
By geography, the US was 39.9% of revenue and contributed 1.6pp, against 0.2pp from non-US markets [D523][D525][D484].
EMEA operating income rose to $4.3 billion on 4% concentrate volume growth and pricing, partly offset by higher commodity costs and a 5% currency headwind [S50][P10].
Operating costs grew 9.7pp slower than revenue in FY2025 [D474], and operating income grew 37.7% against revenue growth of 1.9% [D450][D449].
Diluted EPS grew 23.6% against net income growth of 23.3% as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 is the window high, above the 26.0% median and the 20.7% low [F50][D765][D766][D764].
The 7.5pp operating-margin gain [D463] came mostly from the 6.2pp residual other-lines effect, with cost of revenue adding 0.6pp and SG&A 0.7pp [D477][D475][D476].
The residual reflects lower other operating charges, chiefly the prior-year fairlife remeasurement, plus lower commodity and marketing costs [P6][P12].
In FY2025 net margin of 27.3% sat 1.4pp below the 28.7% operating margin, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [F70][F50][D810][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion was 0.57x net income in FY2025, below the 1.18x window median, and free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x [F100][F60][D436][D800][F120][D437].
FY2024 conversion collapsed to 0.64x [D386] on a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit and refranchising effects [P22].
Free cash flow margin of 11.0% is near the 10.1% window low and far below the 20.2% median [D433][D773][D775].
Capex was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A in FY2025 [D432][D438], so capital intensity has risen against depreciation.
The pack's last net cash figure is FY2023 net debt of $32.4 billion, -70.7% of revenue, because long-term debt is not reported after FY2023 [D341][D342][X194].
Cash and investments of $10.3 billion in FY2025 understate the filer's total by $3.6 billion of unmapped short-term investments [D440][R11].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, above the $5.3 billion of free cash flow [D444][D445][F120].
Return on average equity of 46.0% ranks at the 67th percentile against a 36.5% peer median [D448][D797][D798].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion against $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [F2][X2][F3][X3][R1].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2017-FY2018 comparisons should not be read as filed [R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 105.1%, 214.2% and 179.9% [D344][D395][D445][R2].
Payout above free cash flow for three years means capital return is being funded from the balance sheet rather than internally generated cash [R2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [D387][D437][R3].
That gap is the weakest conversion in the window and sits at the 0th percentile against a 0.94x peer median [D776][D795][D796].
Whether operating cash flow divided by net income recovers above the 1.18x window median from 0.57x in FY2025 [D436][D800], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating margin holds above the 26.0% window median after the 28.7% FY2025 high, which leaned on the 6.2pp other-lines effect [F50][D766][D477], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether buybacks plus dividends fall back below the 105.1% FY2023 level from 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D344][D445], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
